strengths: Addresses an important but understudied vulnerability in safety-critical DNS systems (hearing aids, emergency communications, ATC)
Comprehensive experimental coverage: 4 models, diverse SNR/reverb settings, over-the-air simulation with real RIRs, multiple metrics
Psychoacoustically principled attack methodology with rigorous masking enhancements (temporal pre/post-masking, threshold offsets)
Human validation with transcription and ABX studies demonstrating unintelligibility and marginal imperceptibility
Excellent reproducibility: multiple seeds (20), detailed hyperparameters, promised code/samples, honest reporting of negative results
Valuable mechanistic insight: FSN+ robustness comes from gradient instability (pseudo-robustness) rather than architecture
Results generalize across diverse conditions (70 dB near-clean to -10 dB noisy, with/without reverb)
Methodologically rigorous: proper statistical tests (two-way bootstrap with crossed effects), ablations validating design choices
weaknesses: Methodological novelty is incremental: core approach (PGD + psychoacoustic masking) closely follows Qin et al. [38] and Schönherr et al. [45]; main contributions are domain adaptation and STOI as loss, which are engineering-level rather than algorithmic innovations

Practical threat model is significantly constrained: attacks require white-box access; naive transfer fails across architectures; weak cross-checkpoint transfer even within same model family; pure black-box attacks not thoroughly explored

Human study limitations substantially weaken imperceptibility claims: small sample (n=15 from single lab), ABX results statistically marginal (59% mean with 95% CI lower bound 0.478, not significantly above 50% chance), only 3/4 models evaluated, 5-second clips shorter than typical conversations

Targeted attacks are largely unsuccessful: STOI metric breaks down as maximization objective; subjective evaluation reveals targets barely audible even at high STOI; cross-speaker and synthesized targets ineffective
Over-the-air attacks only simulated: real playback chains introduce nonlinearities, gain control, codec compression not modeled; no actual over-the-air validation experiments

Defense analysis is superficial: only Gaussian noise baseline evaluated; no adversarial training or principled defenses; Gaussian noise already moderately effective, limiting impact of security findings

Limited mechanistic understanding: paper documents vulnerability but provides minimal insight into why DNS models fail to reject adversarial noise; no analysis of what architectural properties or training procedures would improve robustness
Metric-specific results: attack success varies across metrics (Figure 11); STOI chosen partly due to PESQ licensing issue; unclear which metric best captures intelligibility
